definition: A patch lies closer to A when its farmland is dominated by fewer, wider, more expansive parcels. It lies closer to B when farmland is divided into many thin, elongated strips with closely spaced parallel boundaries. Judge parcel geometry across the patch rather than crop color.
cues: A has wider, blockier fields; B has more long, narrow ribbons.
B shows denser sequences of parallel field boundaries and alternating crop or soil bands.
A more often contains broad, uninterrupted field interiors with mottled texture.
